## TL;DR

I drove the task worktree’s auth-less server through every Settings tab and every Agents page tab. The pages rendered their expected controls and status information, and I found one environment-dependent model refresh warning with a saved-list fallback. I could not verify the acceptance criterion that every control saves, validates, and survives reload: `just serve-noauth` runs as a read-only preview child, and the server rejects all write requests. I did not bypass that guard or point a writer at project configuration. I recorded the observations and limitation in `docs/qa/2026-11-settings-agents.md`. No product bug was confirmed, so no implementation or bug-specific test was added.

## Work and rationale

The task asked for a broad QA pass across Settings and Agents, not a redesign. I used the documented `just serve-noauth 7272` command from this dedicated worktree, checked that the app reported the task branch and preview mode, and used Chrome to inspect the app. I viewed General and all its section links, Notifications, Security, Advanced, Import/Export, Support, and the raw `repoos.toml` tab. I also opened Agents, Build Your Team, Scheduled Tasks, Reminders, Detected Coding Agents, Model Playground, Model providers, Budget Controls, and Model routing.

I treated controls that would affect credentials, notifications, shared budget policy, external AI calls, scheduled task creation, or repository state as read-only. In particular, I did not send a Model Playground prompt, run a provider connection test, toggle Telegram or browser push, alter a saved key, change budget pause state, or enable schedules. These actions could transmit information, create side effects, or change shared state. I made no config changes and did not edit `repoos.toml`.

On Notifications, I attempted to enter a negative spend-alert threshold to check the form’s invalid-input behavior. The preview server’s router rejected writes globally; the value stayed at zero and the Settings page displayed “Preview servers are read-only.” That is the concrete blocker: even a safe disposable threshold could not be saved or persisted on this server. The isolated preview config overlay does not remove the preview API’s write prohibition. I did not bypass the route guard or run a writable server against project configuration.

The Agents state was readable. The default roles and custom agent were listed. Cursor model refresh showed an authentication-required warning and retained the saved model list, so this was recorded as an environment condition rather than a proven persistence defect. Model routing showed Shadow mode, OpenRouter, a saved key state, and provider readiness without exposing the secret. Other tabs showed current schedules, reminders, detected CLIs, provider status, and budget state. The Model Playground send action remained untouched because testing it would send codebase context to an external model provider.

No independent bug could be established from read-only observation. Accordingly, there is no code change to test and no claim that the save/reload criterion passed. The QA note separates inspected UI state from the unverified write behavior and records what should be tested in a writable, isolated config environment.

## Approaches tried

I started the documented auth-less preview in the task worktree and confirmed the page rendered at the branch’s local URL. I inspected accessible UI state tab by tab. I also attempted a negative input on the spend-alert stepper. The server displayed its read-only-preview status and prevented the state from changing. A direct writable test would require a separate isolated config root; the provided command did not offer that mode. Bypassing preview mode would weaken the intended write boundary, so I stopped at the blocked test rather than making an unsafe change.

I ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` before writing the QA note. The remote validation runner passed the build, scoped test suite, and browser gate; local format, lint, build, and UI smoke checks passed. After writing the QA note, I ran the same command again. RepoOS classified the diff as documentation-only, passed the applicable bookkeeping checks, and skipped the full build/test path by plan.

## Challenges and blockers

The preview child makes its API read-only by design. It can display effective config, but it rejects non-GET/HEAD requests, preventing a real save and reload check on any Settings control. The user explicitly excluded the main checkout and real config from this task, and I did not create an alternate writable root. As a result, acceptance remains incomplete for save, validation, and persistence after reload. Support’s private diagnostics preview also remained in its “Preparing a private bundle preview” state during navigation; I did not create or upload a bundle, so this was recorded as an observation without calling it a confirmed bug.

## Key learnings

A rendered form and a successful read-only config fetch do not prove that a setting saves. For QA that exercises server-backed Settings controls, the harness needs a disposable writable config root with the same schema and routes, or a supported test mode that allows config writes without touching the real project config. Keep the read-only preview guard intact: it safely supports UI inspection, but it cannot serve as evidence for persistence. Distinguish provider authentication errors from bad saved state when the UI explicitly falls back to the saved list.
